meta.subtitle: Lesson 18 – Word order: time and place

sentences.nl: Dit is Lars.
sentences.en: This is Lars.

sentences.nl: Lars is een vriend van Martin.
sentences.en: Lars is a friend of Martin.

sentences.nl: Hij woont in Zweden.
sentences.en: He lives in Sweden.

sentences.nl: Lars leert Nederlands.
sentences.en: Lars is learning Dutch.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Lars learns Dutch.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence follows a simple Subject-Verb-Object (SVO) structure: "Lars" (subject) + "leert" (verb) + "Nederlands" (object).  
• The verb "leert" is in the present tense, which is used for actions happening now or general truths.  
• "Nederlands" is the noun for the Dutch language. Note that language names in Dutch are capitalized.

• Extra phrases/sentences:  
  - "Zij leert Engels." (She learns English.)  
  - "Wij leren Spaans." (We learn Spanish.)  
  - "Jullie leren Frans." (You all learn French.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Anja leert Duits." (Anja learns German.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Learning Dutch can be an important step for integration in the Netherlands, where language skills are valued for both social and professional interactions.

sentences.nl: Lars gaat een cursus in Nederland boeken.
sentences.en: Lars is going to book a course in the Netherlands.

sentences.nl: Hij zit op de website van de Dutch Summer School.
sentences.en: He is on the website of the Dutch Summer School.

sentences.nl: Lars heeft nog een paar vragen en belt de organisatie.
sentences.en: Lars has a few more questions and calls the organization.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Lars has still a few questions and calls the organization.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses "nog" to mean "still" or "yet," indicating that Lars continues to have questions.  
• "Een paar" is a common way to say "a few" in Dutch.  
• The verb "belt" is in the present tense, indicating a current action.  
• Word order follows the typical SVO (Subject-Verb-Object) pattern, even with the conjunction "en" (and) connecting two independent clauses.

• Example: "Ik heb nog steeds geen idee." (I still have no idea.)  
• Example: "Zij koopt een paar boeken voor de vakantie." (She buys a few books for the vacation.)  
• Example: "Hij belt zijn moeder elke zondag." (He calls his mother every Sunday.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Lisa heeft nog wat tijd en leest het boek. (Lisa still has some time and reads the book.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, asking questions and seeking clarification is often encouraged, reflecting the Dutch value of direct communication.

sentences.nl: BLC Language Courses, met Bart.
sentences.en: BLC Language Courses, with Bart.

sentences.nl: Hallo, ik ben Lars uit Malmˆ in Zweden.
sentences.en: Hello, I am Lars from Malmö in Sweden.

sentences.nl: Dag Lars, waarmee kan ik je helpen? — Ik wil volgend jaar in de zomer, in de eerste helft van juli een cursus Nederlands doen.
sentences.en: Hello Lars, how can I help you? — I want to take a Dutch course next year in the summer, in the first half of July.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Day Lars, with-what can I you help? — I want next year in the summer, in the first half of July a course Dutch do.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Waarmee kan ik je helpen?" is a standard phrase meaning "How can I help you?" The word "waarmee" translates to "with what," showing the use of prepositions in questions.  
• "Volgend jaar" means "next year." The adjective comes before the noun, which is a common structure.  
• "In de eerste helft van juli" translates to "in the first half of July," showing the use of definite articles and prepositions to indicate time.

Extra examples:  
• "Waarmee kan ik u van dienst zijn?" (How can I be of service to you?)  
• "Volgend jaar gaan we naar Frankrijk." (Next year we are going to France.)  
• "In de tweede helft van augustus ben ik op vakantie." (In the second half of August, I am on vacation.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Ik wil graag in het voorjaar een nieuwe taal leren." (I would like to learn a new language in spring.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• None

sentences.nl: Maar ik heb nog een paar vragen.
sentences.en: But I still have a few questions.

sentences.nl: Geen probleem.
sentences.en: No problem.

sentences.nl: Ik beantwoord graag al jouw vragen.
sentences.en: I am happy to answer all your questions.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• I answer gladly all your questions.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The verb "beantwoord" is in the present tense and comes from "beantwoorden," meaning "to answer."  
• "Graag" is used to express preference or willingness, similar to "gladly" or "would like to."  
• The sentence follows a Subject-Verb-Object order, typical in Dutch when there's no inversion.  

• Examples:  
  - Zij kookt graag Italiaanse gerechten. (She likes to cook Italian dishes.)  
  - Wij helpen graag met het project. (We gladly help with the project.)  
  - Hij leest graag boeken over geschiedenis. (He enjoys reading books about history.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Wij beantwoorden graag al jouw e-mails. (We gladly answer all your emails.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
-

sentences.nl: Mijn eerste vraag: waar is de cursus op het platteland? — Die cursus is op een vakantiepark, op tien kilometer van treinstation Beilen, in de provincie Drenthe.
sentences.en: My first question: where is the course in the countryside? — That course is at a holiday park, ten kilometers from Beilen train station, in the province of Drenthe.

sentences.nl: Hoeveel kost een cursus? — De prijzen van de cursus staan op de website.
sentences.en: How much does a course cost? — The course prices are on the website.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• How much costs a course? — The prices of the course stand on the website.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Hoeveel kost" is a common way to ask about the price of something, using the verb "kosten" (to cost) in a question format.  
• "De prijzen van de cursus" uses a possessive structure with "van" to indicate the prices belonging to the course.  
• "Staan op de website" uses the verb "staan" (to stand) to mean "are located on" or "can be found on" the website.

• Extra phrases/sentences:  
  - Hoeveel kost de fiets? (How much does the bike cost?)  
  - De openingstijden van de winkel staan op de deur. (The opening hours of the shop are on the door.)  
  - De locatie van het evenement staat in de uitnodiging. (The location of the event is in the invitation.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Hoeveel kost het boek? — De details van het boek staan in de catalogus. (How much does the book cost? — The details of the book are in the catalog.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, many services and courses are often listed online, and it's common practice to check the website for pricing and details before making inquiries.

sentences.nl: Maar hoe weet ik het totaalbedrag inclusief huisvesting? — Klik op de knop ‘prijscalculatie’, rechtsboven op de website.
sentences.en: But how do I know the total amount including accommodation? — Click on the 'price calculation' button at the top right of the website.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• But how know I the total amount including housing? — Click on the button ‘price calculation’, top right on the website.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Maar hoe weet ik" ("But how do I know") uses inverted word order typical in questions. The verb "weet" comes before the subject "ik".  
• "het totaalbedrag inclusief huisvesting" ("the total amount including housing") shows noun use with an adjective and prepositional phrase. "Inclusief" is a preposition meaning "including".  
• "Klik op de knop" ("Click on the button") is an imperative form, where the verb "klik" is at the start, addressing the listener directly.  

Additional examples:  
• "Hoe vind ik de juiste route?" (How do I find the right route?)  
• "Inclusief ontbijt en diner." (Including breakfast and dinner.)  
• "Druk op de knop om te starten." (Press the button to start.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Hoe bereken ik de kosten inclusief belastingen?" (How do I calculate the costs including taxes?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Websites in Dutch often use English loanwords like "klik" and "website," reflecting a blend of languages in tech contexts.

sentences.nl: Je moet nu het formulier invullen.
sentences.en: You need to fill out the form now.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• You must now the form fill out.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Je moet" means "you must," using the modal verb "moeten" which indicates necessity.  
• "Nu" means "now," showing immediacy or current time.  
• "Het formulier" is "the form," with "het" being the definite article for neuter nouns.  
• "Invullen" means "fill out," a separable verb where "in" (in) and "vullen" (fill) come apart in some tenses.

Extra phrases:  
• "Je moet het boek lezen." (You must read the book.)  
• "Zij moet morgen vroeg opstaan." (She must get up early tomorrow.)  
• "Wij moeten de rekening betalen." (We must pay the bill.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Je moet nu je huiswerk maken." (You must do your homework now.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, filling out forms is common in many aspects of life, such as for government services, healthcare, and education. It's important to complete them accurately and promptly to avoid any delays or issues.

sentences.nl: Dan krijg je een offerte met totaalbedrag per e-mail.
sentences.en: Then you will receive a quote with the total amount by email.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Then receive you a quote with total amount per e-mail.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Dan krijg je" uses the inversion structure common in Dutch, where the verb precedes the subject after a time adverb like "dan" (then).  
• "Een offerte" means "a quote" and is a common business term.  
• "Met totaalbedrag" combines "met" (with) and "totaalbedrag" (total amount), showing how prepositions are used to link objects.  

Extra phrases:  
• "Dan ga je naar huis." (Then you go home.)  
• "Je krijgt een factuur per post." (You get an invoice by mail.)  
• "Ik ontvang de documenten met uitleg." (I receive the documents with explanation.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Dan stuur ik je een uitnodiging voor het feest per post." (Then I send you an invitation for the party by mail.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
(There is no cultural note applicable here.)

sentences.nl: En hoe boek ik de cursus? — Boeken is eenvoudig:, gewoon klikken op de link in het mailtje…, en dan weer alles invullen en de reservering bevestigen.
sentences.en: And how do I book the course? — Booking is simple: just click on the link in the email..., then fill in everything again and confirm the reservation.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And how book I the course? — Booking is simple: just click on the link in the email…, and then again everything fill in and the reservation confirm.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Boek ik" is present tense with subject-verb inversion, common in questions ("Hoe boek ik...?").  
• "Boeken" is an infinitive verb meaning 'to book'.  
• "Gewoon klikken op" uses the verb "klikken" with the preposition "op" to mean 'click on'.  
• "Invullen" means 'to fill in', often used with forms or documents.  
• Example 1: "Hoe vind ik de weg naar het station?" (How do I find the way to the station?)  
• Example 2: "Gewoon volgen de borden." (Just follow the signs.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "En hoe reserveer ik een tafel?" — "Reserveren is simpel: gewoon bellen naar het restaurant en je naam doorgeven." (And how do I reserve a table? — Reserving is simple: just call the restaurant and give your name.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• No related culture notes.

sentences.nl: En hoe betaal ik? — Betalen kan online, met een creditcard of met iDeal.
sentences.en: And how do I pay? — Payment can be made online, with a credit card or with iDeal.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And how pay I? — Paying can online, with a credit card or with iDeal.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The construction "En hoe betaal ik?" uses inversion common in questions, where the verb precedes the subject.  
• "Betalen kan online" uses a modal-like construction where "kan" (can) is used to indicate possibility or capability.  
• "Met een creditcard" and "met iDeal" both use the preposition "met" (with) to indicate the means by which the action is performed.  
• Example 1: "Hoe laat begint de film?" (What time does the movie start?)  
• Example 2: "Je kunt betalen met contant geld." (You can pay with cash.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Hoe reis ik naar het centrum? — Reizen kan met de tram of te voet." (How do I travel to the center? — Traveling can be done by tram or on foot.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• iDeal is a popular online payment system in the Netherlands, commonly used for online shopping and transactions.

sentences.nl: Wat is iDeal? iDeal is een betaalmethode van Nederlandse banken.
sentences.en: What is iDeal? iDeal is a payment method from Dutch banks.

sentences.nl: Heb je een Nederlandse bankrekening? — Eh… nee.
sentences.en: Do you have a Dutch bank account? — Uh… no.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Have you a Dutch bank account? — Uh… no.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses inversion, which is common in Dutch questions: "Heb je" (Have you) instead of "Je hebt" (You have).  
• "Een" is an indefinite article meaning "a" or "an."  
• "Nederlandse" is an adjective meaning "Dutch," modifying "bankrekening" (bank account).  
• Examples:  
  - Heb je een hond? (Do you have a dog?)  
  - Hebben jullie tijd voor koffie? (Do you all have time for coffee?)  
  - Heeft hij zijn boek gelezen? (Has he read his book?)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Heb je een goed boek gelezen? (Have you read a good book?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, having a Dutch bank account is often necessary for everyday transactions, as many places prefer or only accept Dutch debit cards (PIN cards).

sentences.nl: Dan zijn er 2 opties:, creditcard of bankoverschrijving.
sentences.en: Then there are 2 options: credit card or bank transfer.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Then are there 2 options: credit card or bank transfer.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence begins with "Dan," which functions as an adverb meaning "then" or "in that case," indicating a sequence or condition.  
• "Zijn er" is an inverted word order often used in Dutch when starting a sentence with an adverb or another element; it translates to "there are."  
• "Opties" is the plural form of "optie," meaning "option."  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Daar zijn er 3 mogelijkheden." (There are 3 possibilities there.)  
  - "Nu zijn er geen vragen meer." (Now there are no more questions.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Na het eten zijn er 4 desserts om uit te kiezen." (After the meal, there are 4 desserts to choose from.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Credit cards are not as commonly used in the Netherlands as in some other countries. Dutch people often prefer debit cards or direct bank transfers for payments.

sentences.nl: Ik heb een creditcard.
sentences.en: I have a credit card.

sentences.nl: Heeft jouw creditcard een 3-D secure code? — Zijn dat de 3 cijfers op de achterkant van de creditcard? — Nee.
sentences.en: Does your credit card have a 3-D secure code? — Are those the 3 digits on the back of the credit card? — No.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Has your credit card a 3-D secure code? — Are those the 3 numbers on the back of the credit card? — No.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The verb "heeft" (has) is in the present tense and comes first because it's a yes/no question.  
• "3-D secure code" is a specific term related to online security for credit cards.  
• "Zijn dat" (are those) is a question format where the verb "zijn" (are) precedes the subject "dat" (those).  
• "Op de achterkant" means "on the back," using the preposition "op" (on).

Examples:  
- Heeft zij een rijbewijs? (Does she have a driver's license?)  
- Zijn dat jouw sleutels? (Are those your keys?)  
- De code staat op de voorkant van het kaartje. (The code is on the front of the card.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Heeft jouw telefoon een vingerafdrukscanner? (Does your phone have a fingerprint scanner?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The 3-D Secure code is an additional security measure for online transactions with credit cards, commonly used in the Netherlands and other countries to prevent fraud.

sentences.nl: Dat is de CVC code.
sentences.en: That is the CVC code.

sentences.nl: De 3-D secure code, is niet hetzelfde als de CVC code.
sentences.en: The 3-D secure code is not the same as the CVC code.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• The 3-D secure code, is not the same as the CVC code.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• This sentence uses a simple structure with a subject ("De 3-D secure code"), a verb ("is"), and a comparison using "niet hetzelfde als" (not the same as).  
• "Niet hetzelfde als" is a common way to express that one thing is different from another.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Deze auto is niet hetzelfde als die." (This car is not the same as that one.)  
  - "Zijn huis is niet hetzelfde als het jouwe." (His house is not the same as yours.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Deze koffie is niet hetzelfde als die van gisteren. (This coffee is not the same as yesterday's.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, online security is taken very seriously, and many people are familiar with terms like "3-D secure code" and "CVC code" as they are often used in online transactions.

sentences.nl: De 3-D secure code is een extra verificatie.
sentences.en: The 3-D secure code is an extra verification.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• The 3-D secure code is an extra verification.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses the definite article "de" for "code," which is common for masculine and feminine nouns.  
• "3-D secure code" is treated as a noun phrase, with "3-D" as an adjective describing "secure code."  
• "Is" is the third-person singular form of "zijn" (to be), linking the subject to the complement.  
• "Een" is an indefinite article meaning "an" or "a," used before "extra verificatie."

Extra examples:  
• De PIN-code is een noodzakelijke beveiliging. (The PIN code is a necessary security measure.)  
• De online betaling is een snelle transactie. (The online payment is a quick transaction.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• De QR-code is een handige technologie. (The QR code is a handy technology.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The 3-D Secure code is a security protocol used in the Netherlands and many other countries for online transactions, providing an additional layer of security.

sentences.nl: In sommige landen, zoals de Verenigde Staten,, hebben veel creditcards geen 3-D secure code.
sentences.en: In some countries, such as the United States, many credit cards do not have a 3-D secure code.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• In some countries, such as the United States, have many credit cards no 3-D secure code.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• **In sommige landen**: "In" is a preposition meaning "in." "Sommige" is a plural indefinite pronoun meaning "some." "Landen" is a plural noun meaning "countries."  
• **Zoals de Verenigde Staten**: "Zoals" means "such as" or "like." It introduces an example.  
• **Hebben veel creditcards**: "Hebben" is the plural form of the verb "to have." The subject "veel creditcards" (many credit cards) follows the verb because of the sentence's structure.  
• **Geen 3-D secure code**: "Geen" is a negative article used before nouns to mean "no" or "not any."

Examples:  
– In sommige steden regent het vaak. (In some cities, it rains often.)  
– Zoals je ziet, is het huis blauw. (As you see, the house is blue.)  
– Hebben jullie geen tijd? (Do you have no time?)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• In vele winkels, zoals die in Amsterdam, accepteren ze geen contant geld. (In many stores, such as those in Amsterdam, they do not accept cash.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The use of credit cards and the presence of 3-D secure codes can vary widely by country. In the United States, it's common for credit cards not to have this extra security feature, whereas in many European countries, it is more commonly used for online transactions.

sentences.nl: In Nederlandse webwinkels kun je niet betalen, zonder die 3-D secure code.
sentences.en: In Dutch online stores, you cannot pay without that 3-D secure code.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• In Dutch webshops can you not pay, without that 3-D secure code.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The word order "kun je niet betalen" reflects the typical Dutch structure where the modal verb "kun" (can) is followed by the subject "je" (you), then the negation "niet" (not), and finally the main verb "betalen" (pay).  
• "Zonder die 3-D secure code" uses "zonder" (without), which is a preposition, and it requires the noun phrase "die 3-D secure code" to follow it directly.  
• Example 1: "In sommige landen kun je niet rijden zonder rijbewijs." (In some countries, you can't drive without a driver's license.)  
• Example 2: "Je kunt niet naar binnen zonder kaartje." (You can't enter without a ticket.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• In veel bibliotheken kun je niet lenen zonder bibliotheekpas. (In many libraries, you can't borrow without a library card.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, the use of secure payment methods like 3-D Secure is common for online transactions. This is a security measure to help prevent fraud, and many Dutch consumers are accustomed to using these codes when shopping online.

sentences.nl: OK.
sentences.en: OK.

sentences.nl: Alles is duidelijk.
sentences.en: Everything is clear.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Everything is clear.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Alles" means "everything" and serves as the subject of the sentence.  
• "Is" is the present tense of the verb "zijn" (to be), used here as a linking verb.  
• "Duidelijk" is an adjective meaning "clear." In Dutch, adjectives follow the verb when used in a predicate position.  
• Word order in Dutch typically follows Subject-Verb-Object (SVO) for simple statements.  

Extra phrases:  
- "Alles is mogelijk." (Everything is possible.)  
- "Het is duidelijk." (It is clear.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Niets is verloren." (Nothing is lost.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• None

sentences.nl: Dan praten we over reizen en het openbaar vervoer.
sentences.en: Then we talk about travel and public transport.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Then talk we about travel and the public transport.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence begins with "Dan" (Then), which can indicate a time or sequence.  
• "Praten we over" (talk we about) follows a typical Dutch word order where the subject (we) follows the verb (praten) in a main clause introduced by an element like "Dan."  
• "Reizen en het openbaar vervoer" (travel and the public transport) is a compound object of the preposition "over."  
• Extra examples:  
  - "Dan eten we om zes uur." (Then we eat at six o'clock.)  
  - "Daarna praten we over het weer." (Afterwards we talk about the weather.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Dan kijken we naar de film en eten we popcorn." (Then we watch the movie and eat popcorn.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Public transport, especially trains, is a common topic of conversation in the Netherlands as it is widely used and integral to daily commuting and travel.

dit.spelling: The short vowel /ɪ/ is followed by a voiceless plosive /t/, typical of closed syllables.
dit.fast: In rapid speech, the /t/ in ‘dit is’ can become a flap [ɾ] or be elided entirely.

een.spelling: The article ‘een’ is pronounced with a long /eː/ to distinguish it from the numeral ‘één’, which has a stressed pronunciation.
een.fast: In rapid speech, ‘een’ may be reduced to a schwa sound /ən/ when it is unstressed.

vriend.spelling: The initial cluster 'vr-' is common in Dutch, and the final '-d' is pronounced as /t/.
vriend.fast: In rapid speech, the final /t/ in 'vriend' may be less pronounced or even dropped when followed by a word starting with a consonant.

van.spelling: The short vowel /ɑ/ is common in monosyllabic words ending in -n.
van.fast: The final /n/ in ‘van’ is often elided in casual speech, particularly before consonants.

martin.spelling: The /ɑ/ in the first syllable is a short vowel due to the closed syllable pattern.
martin.fast: In connected speech, the /n/ at the end of ‘martin’ may assimilate to a nasalized vowel before a following vowel sound.

nederlands.spelling: The 'ee' in 'nee' is a long vowel /eː/ and the 'a' in 'lands' is a short vowel /ɑ/.
nederlands.fast: In rapid speech, the final /ts/ in 'nederlands' may be reduced, causing it to blend with following words.
